name: SOAS University of London
aliases: School of Oriental and African Studies

settingEvidence.evidence: Explore our city-centre campus located in the heart of the Bloomsbury quarter, with a world-class research Library, international gallery and modern student facilities.

fees.text: £10,050 a year for Home (UK) students in 2027/28, the Home fee cap the UK government has announced (it is £9,790 in 2026/27). SOAS says 2028/29 fees are not announced yet but are likely to rise by 2-4%. A Year in Industry or a year abroad costs £1,425 for Home students in 2026/27.

livingCosts.text: Undergraduate halls cost about £185 to £431 a week in 2026/27 depending on the hall and room (cheapest: single rooms at Wood Green Hall from £185; the dearest listed is the catered ensuite at Garden Halls at about £431). Contract lengths vary from 38 to 51 weeks, which changes the weekly price.

openDays.text: No undergraduate open days are listed yet: SOAS's open days page currently lists only a Postgraduate Open House (1 December 2026). You can book an in-person campus tour instead.

contextual.summary: UK applicants who meet at least one of SOAS's contextual criteria can be considered for a contextual offer with reduced grades.
contextual.typicalReduction: Up to two grades below the standard entry requirements (the Economics course pages list BBB against a standard ABB)

criteria.detail: Free School Meals (listed as an example of the contextual data SOAS may take into account).
POLAR4: how likely young people in your area are to go to higher education (SOAS does not say which quintiles count).
IMD: how deprived your area in England is (SOAS does not say which quintiles count).
Parent or carer in armed forces.

contextual.rulesText: The criteria are examples of the contextual data SOAS may take into account. Applicants must meet at least one of them to be considered for a contextual offer. Contextual offers are not made for BTEC qualifications or A levels combined with other qualifications, or through Clearing.

source.evidence: Applicants must meet at least one of the above criteria to be considered for a contextual offer.

programmes.name: SOAS Year 12 Outreach Summer School
programmes.summary: A free week-long, non-residential summer school at SOAS for Year 12 students, with a 'Thriving futures' pathway on Economics, Finance and Global Development.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students attending state schools and colleges. Students who are eligible or were previously eligible for Free School Meals, have experience of local authority care, or come from an area underrepresented in higher education (TUNDRA) are prioritised.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Open to Year 12 students at state schools and colleges; places are prioritised for students who meet at least one of: eligible or previously eligible for Free School Meals; experience of local authority care; from an area underrepresented in higher education (measured by TUNDRA).
benefits: Free; SOAS covers travel costs for eligible students who live outside the London Oyster Card 16+ Travel Zones
Lectures by leading academics, study skills sessions and information about university life and UCAS
Meet recent graduates and current SOAS students and complete a group project
programmes.subjects: Thriving futures pathway: Economics, Finance and Global Development (other pathways: Cross-cultural connections; Law and society)

runs.text: Expected mid-July 2027 (the 2026 summer school ran 13 to 17 July 2026, 10:00 to 16:00)

deadline.text: Not published for 2027 yet (the 2026 deadline was 9:00am on Friday 24 April 2026)

programmes.infoNote: Based on the 2026 programme (13 to 17 July 2026; applications closed 24 April 2026). 2027 dates are not announced yet; the Expected timing is based on the 2026 dates.

programmes.name: Economics Masterclass for Years 12 and 13: the £3.50 coffee

programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 and 13 students at state schools, academies and colleges; students who meet at least one of the priority criteria are prioritised. School/college and parent or guardian permission is needed.

benefits: Free Economics masterclass led by SOAS Department of Economics staff
Campus tour and a higher education workshop led by Student Ambassadors

SOAS is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry and none of the Economics course pages names an admissions test.

BSc Economics needs A-level Maths at grade B or above. BA Economics, BSc Development Economics, BSc Accounting and Finance, BSc Management and the Economics two-subject degrees ask for GCSE Maths grade 6/B if you do not have A-level Maths.
SOAS's Economics department describes itself as specialising in political economy, heterodox (non-mainstream) approaches and the economics of development.
Students who do not meet the entry requirements can take SOAS's 4-year integrated Foundation Year (Home fee £5,760 in 2026/27) and then progress onto any undergraduate programme.

EPQ: SOAS takes an EPQ into consideration if you take it alongside 3 A levels, are predicted at least a B in it and your A-level predictions meet the entry requirements; it does not publish a lower offer for it.
SOAS runs on-campus masterclasses for Year 12 and 13 throughout the year; its page for schools says to sign up to its Access and Participation newsletter for teachers and advisers.
